input.text: You've reached the Beijing Zoo — China's oldest zoo, opening in nineteen zero six as an imperial experiment garden, and home to its most beloved ambassadors: the giant pandas. The Panda House is the heart of any visit — watch the bears do what they do best: eating bamboo, up to twelve hours a day, or simply tumbling around like living plush toys. Come in the morning, when they're most active and the crowds are thinnest. But the zoo is more than pandas: over ninety years as a public zoo, it grew into one of the world's largest, with golden monkeys, red pandas, and a lakeside setting that makes it as much park as menagerie. Families could spend half a day here; panda-only pilgrims can be done in two hours. One rule applies everywhere: quiet voices, patient eyes — the stars perform on their own schedule.
